rationale: The Court is likely to reject the Sixth Circuit’s categorical “any-crime” bar and adopt a charge-specific Fourth Amendment inquiry for seizures pursuant to legal process, while requiring proof that the baseless charge caused incremental restraint (or other legally cognizable injury) beyond what the supported charge would have produced. Roberts is best positioned to write a narrow, administrable opinion synthesizing Manuel/Thompson with ordinary § 1983 causation limits, with a likely Thomas and/or Alito dissent emphasizing seizure-as-a-whole reasonableness and skepticism of charge-by-charge constitutionalization.
